title: A towel twice as thick
hook: Same size, twice as thick, twice the water. Does it get more face to dry from?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that doubling a towel's thickness doubles the water it holds but not the face area the water leaves through, so it dries slower

misconception: A thick towel dries about as fast as a thin one of the same size.
objective: Doubling thickness at the same width and length doubles material volume while keeping the two large face areas fixed. The area-to-volume ratio therefore halves.

claims.text: Doubling thickness at the same width and length doubles material volume while keeping the two large face areas fixed. The area-to-volume ratio therefore halves.

recall.question: A 50 × 100 cm cloth goes from 2 mm to 4 mm thick. What happens to its face-area-to-volume ratio?
recall.why: The two large faces stay 50 × 100 cm each while the volume doubles with thickness, so the ratio halves. The ratio alone does not set a drying time.
